summary: MPP binds the challenge id to every defined challenge parameter except the human-readable description, makes ids and proofs single use, forbids side effects before payment and requires TLS, so tampering and replay are covered at protocol level. What it leaves to clients is deciding whether a challenge is honest, because a malicious server can bind a bad price as easily as a good one. Credentials are bearer tokens. Loss limits, refunds and disputes come from the rail. As of 2026-10-21 the MPP SDK repositories had published nine security advisories, all for SDK bugs and all fixed: five for mppx, two for the Rust crate mpp and two for pympp. Outside finders reported them, and none reports exploitation. A formal analysis posted on 2026-08-30 counts 12 previously undocumented formal-consistency cases for MPP, which its authors say are not demonstrated vulnerabilities in production deployments. Advisory dates below are the dates each repository published the advisory.

threats.title: Malicious or spoofed server asks for the wrong payment
threats.description: A server, a mirror or an injected tool result issues a validly bound challenge that names its own recipient or an inflated amount, with a reassuring description.
preconditions: The client pays whatever a challenge asks
No recipient allowlist or price ceiling
threats.impact: The client pays the attacker; on-chain charges are final.
threats.implementerNotes: Binding only protects a challenge after the server issues it. Clients must check amount, recipient, currency and expires and ignore description, as the core requires; enforce an allowlist before signing. With redirect following turned on, pympp before 0.10.1 could pay a challenge reached through a cross-origin redirect (GHSA-5r9p-36vq-j23h).

threats.title: Leaked bearer credential is spent by someone else
threats.description: A credential copied from logs, an error message, analytics or a proxy is presented before the legitimate client uses it.
preconditions: Credential logged or exposed in transit
threats.impact: Whoever presents it first gets the paid resource; the payer has paid for someone else.
threats.implementerNotes: The core forbids logging credentials and requires TLS 1.2 or later. Keep credentials in memory only and use short expires values.

threats.title: Replay of a consumed challenge or proof
threats.description: The same credential is sent twice, concurrently or later, to obtain service twice or to settle twice.
preconditions: Server does not record consumed ids atomically
Method proof not checked for single use
threats.implementerNotes: Ids are single use and methods must give single-use proofs; concurrent duplicates must settle at most once. mppx and the Rust SDK had replay bugs fixed in 0.4.8, 0.4.11 and 0.8.0, and mppx shipped further replay fixes without an advisory in 0.8.7 and 0.13.2.

threats.title: SPT replay through Stripe idempotency
threats.description: A stripe/charge implementation ignores Stripe's Idempotent-Replayed signal, so one SPT credential pays for several new challenges.
preconditions: Server does not record consumed challenge ids or used SPTs
threats.impact: Seller delivers several times for one payment (CVE-2026-34210).
threats.implementerNotes: Implementation bug, fixed in mppx 0.4.11. The vulnerable code already built the Stripe idempotency key from the challenge id and the SPT, so a replayed credential got Stripe's cached PaymentIntent back and mppx counted it as a new payment. The stripe draft requires servers to enforce single-use challenge ids and to check that an SPT was not used before; treat Idempotent-Replayed as a replay.

threats.title: Session close voucher accepted at the settled amount
threats.description: A close voucher equal to, not above, the settled amount was accepted, so an attacker could close or grief a channel for free.
threats.impact: Payee loses unsettled earnings or the channel is closed against its will (CVE-2026-34209).
threats.implementerNotes: Implementation bug, fixed in mppx 0.4.11. Since 2026-06-25 (pull request 278) the Tempo session draft requires a server to check that a close voucher covers at least the greater of its recorded spent amount and the on-chain settled amount, and in v2 to capture max(spent, settled).

threats.title: Fee payer gas draining
threats.description: When the server sponsors fees, an attacker pads calldata or adds access lists so each sponsored transaction burns more gas than the policy expected.
preconditions: Server mppx before 0.8.2 or pympp before 0.9.1
threats.impact: Server's fee wallet drains (CVE-2026-63627, CVE-2026-63628; GHSA-v858-xh7w-8jr5 in pympp).
threats.implementerNotes: Cap calldata size and reject access lists for sponsored transactions; set a daily ceiling on the fee wallet.

threats.title: Shared cache stores a paid response
threats.description: A proxy or CDN caches a response to a request that used Payment-Authorization, which RFC 9111 does not protect the way it protects Authorization.
threats.impact: Paid content and receipts are served to other users.
threats.implementerNotes: Send no-store on 402 and private on receipts and on any response to a Payment-Authorization request.

threats.title: Spoofed discovery metadata
threats.description: Discovery documents are unauthenticated, so an attacker publishes /openapi.json data with false prices or methods to lure agents.
threats.impact: Agents route to an attacker or overpay.
threats.implementerNotes: Discovery is advisory and must not drive security decisions; the 402 challenge is authoritative.

threats.title: Tempo session liabilities that never end
threats.description: Tempo session channels and vouchers have no expiry, as in the EVM and Hedera session drafts, so deposits stay locked and unsettled vouchers stay claimable until someone closes the channel. Other session methods differ: XRPL channels can carry Expiration or CancelAfter, and Solana sessions add idle timeouts and an optional voucher expiresAt.
threats.impact: Locked funds; late claims surprise the payer.
threats.implementerNotes: Servers should close idle channels; clients should track channels and force-close, waiting at least 16 minutes after requestClose.

threats.title: Disputed delivery after an on-chain charge
threats.description: The client says it never got the resource; on stablecoin rails there is no chargeback and the receipt only proves payment.
preconditions: Server returned an error after settling
threats.impact: Payer bears the loss unless the seller refunds voluntarily.
threats.implementerNotes: The charge intent forbids partial delivery before verification; keep receipts and logs and publish a refund policy. Card routes keep chargebacks.

threats.title: Public settlement reveals payer and payee
threats.description: Tempo and other chain methods settle on public ledgers that explorers index.
threats.impact: Spending patterns and counterparties are visible.
threats.implementerNotes: Use fresh addresses or card and Stripe methods where privacy matters; the core only asks methods to support pseudonymous options.

threats.title: Body swapped after payment
threats.description: A credential for a cheap request body is replayed with a different, more expensive body.
threats.impact: Client gets more than it paid for, or the server does work it did not price.
threats.implementerNotes: Use the digest parameter (RFC 9530) for requests with bodies and an Idempotency-Key.

scenarios.title: A tool result names a different recipient
preconditions: An agent reads 402 responses relayed by a third-party tool
steps: The tool rewrites the challenge from its own server, binding its own recipient
The agent sees a valid challenge and signs a Tempo transfer
The attacker's server returns a receipt for nothing
scenarios.impact: Loss of the payment; no protocol refund on chain.

scenarios.title: Fee wallet drained through sponsored transactions
steps: Each transaction it signs carries padded calldata or a large access list
The server co-signs and pays inflated fees
scenarios.impact: The server's fee balance is spent without matching revenue.

scenarios.title: Server vanishes mid-session
steps: The client's close request times out
The client calls requestClose on chain
The server, if alive, can still settle its newest voucher during the grace period
After at least 15 minutes the client calls withdraw and recovers the rest
scenarios.impact: Funds locked for the grace period; the payer loses at most what the server can still settle with vouchers it holds.

research.title: A Formal Analysis of Agent Payment Protocols
research.finding: Tamarin models of x402, MPP, ACP and AP2. Of its 40 previously undocumented formal-consistency cases, 12 concern MPP (beside 9 known ones), among them MPP-14, where a retry after a lost response counts Tempo session spend twice. The authors say the counts are not demonstrated vulnerabilities in production deployments and that they disclosed their findings to the maintainers.

research.title: SoK: Security of Autonomous LLM Agents in Agentic Commerce
research.finding: A systematization of agent commerce threats that includes MPP in its protocol set.

research.title: Free-Riding the Agentic Web: A Systematic Security Analysis of x402 Payments
research.finding: Four flaw classes in x402 payment binding and delivery: cross-resource substitution, duplicate-settlement races, allowance overdraft and denial of settlement. Version 2 (2026-06-22) names MPP among HTTP 402 payment protocols and as future work for model checking, but tests only x402. Its first two classes resemble the cross-route and concurrent replay bugs that mppx fixed in 0.4.8, under an advisory published on 2026-03-26.

cves.summary: Critical mppx advisory (before 0.4.8): several tempo/charge and tempo/session bypasses, including hash replay across modes and routes, free pull-mode charges, fee payer manipulation and voucher signature bypass. No CVE id.
GHSA-mv9j-8jvg-j8mr: mppx before 0.4.11 accepted a session close voucher equal to the settled amount, closing or griefing a channel for free. Fixed in 0.4.11; NVD published 2026-03-31.

GHSA-8mhj-rffc-rcvw: mppx before 0.4.11 ignored Stripe's Idempotent-Replayed header, so one SPT credential could be replayed. Fixed in 0.4.11; NVD published 2026-03-31. The GitHub Advisory Database rates it medium (CVSS 4.0 score 6.0) and NVD rates it high (CVSS 3.1 score 8.1).
Critical advisory for the Rust crate mpp before 0.8.0: free and replayed charges, griefed sessions, fee payer manipulation and replayed stripe charges. No CVE id.
GHSA-727h-3vm5-qwq6: fee payer gas draining by calldata padding in mppx; fixed in 0.8.2.
GHSA-vc9j-9wph-qghj: fee payer gas draining with access lists in mppx; fixed in 0.8.2.
pympp before 0.9.1: fee payer gas draining by calldata padding, the same attack as CVE-2026-63627 in mppx. Fixed in 0.9.1. The advisory names CVE-2026-63634.

pympp 0.10.0 and earlier: with redirect following turned on, PaymentTransport paid a 402 challenge from a cross-origin redirect target, so an attacker who controlled that target could choose the amount and recipient. The default client does not follow redirects. Fixed in 0.10.1. No CVE id.

Rust crate mpp 0.11.0 and earlier: server middleware could attach a Payment-Receipt to a failed response, and body-aware routes answered a failed verification with a bare 402 and no fresh challenge. Fixed in 0.12.0. No CVE id.
